title: Categorical Exemption from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Public Resources Code section 21080.66, and related CEQA findings;…
text:
[Council File 26-1207; CD 13]
Categorical Exemption from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Public Resources Code section 21080.66, and related CEQA findings; report from the Los Angeles City Planning Commission (LACPC); and an appeal filed by Pat Hadnagy, from the determination of the LACPC in approving, pursuant to Los Angeles Municipal Code Chapter 1 Section 16.05 and Chapter 1A Section 13B.2.4, a Project Review for a project that results in an increase of 50 or more residential dwelling units; for the demolition of five existing carports and accessory structures in an existing residential development with seven residential buildings including 48 existing units on a site spanning 11 lots with 88,773 square feet of lot area, and the construction, use, and maintenance of three new residential buildings, including one four-story building and two five-story buildings, adding a total of 76 new dwelling units, of which six are reserved for very low-income households, the Project will add 71,269 square feet of new floor area for a total Floor Area Ratio of 1.44:1 and 124 dwelling units, the Project will provide 119 parking spaces across three two-level subterranean parking lots in addition to 59 long-term bicycle parking spaces and six short-term bicycle parking spaces, the Project is removing four non-protected on-site trees and will provide 144 trees, and proposes the export of approximately 35,600 cubic yards of soil; for the properties located at 2413–2499 North Silver Lake Boulevard, subject to Modified Conditions of Approval; and adoption of project findings.
Applicant: Fang Qian Morgan, Fang Qian Morgan EGST Trust & Seth, James Morgan EGST Trust
Representative: Gary Benjamin, Alchemy Planning + Land Use
Case No. CPC-2024-5534-DB-PR-VHCA-1A
Environmental No. ENV-2024-5535-SE
Fiscal Impact Statement:
No
Community Impact Statement:
None submitted
TIME LIMIT FILE - NOVEMBER 20, 2026
(LAST DAY FOR COUNCIL ACTION - NOVEMBER 20, 2026)
summary: Appeal of approval for 76 new residential units in three new buildings at 2413–2499 North Silver Lake Boulevard, six of them reserved for very low-income households, alongside the 48 units already on the site.
